column4: NAD+ precursor; raises BubR1 via SIRT2/K668 (North 2014). Human RCT in Werner, paediatric exposure in A-T
the precursor actually used in North 2014; FDA restored supplement status Sept 2025
anti-CD38; CD38 is the principal NAD+-consuming ectoenzyme, so blockade raises NAD+. Surfaced by the search as the ONLY approved drug acting on the abundance tier
the senolytic combination; dasatinib approved with a paediatric indication. Baker 2011 rescued muscle in the BubR1 mouse by clearing p16+ cells
flavonoid senolytic in active trials; oral, low toxicity
BCL-2/BCL-xL inhibitor, surfaced by the search on both BCL2 and BCL2L1
JAK1/2 inhibitor; SASP suppression and frailty rescue in aged mice (Xu 2015)
mTOR inhibitor; SASP translational control. Paediatric use established in vascular anomalies and TSC
geroprotective/senomorphic; paediatric approval from age 10 for type 2 diabetes
HSP90 inhibitor (17-AAG). GATE G1 and G2: depletes the residual mutant BubR1 (Suijkerbuijk 2010) AND is Tang 2011's aneuploidy-selective agent
NAMPT inhibitor. GATE G1: lowers NAD+, the opposite of the intended direction
PARP inhibitor; NAD+-sparing in principle, but genotoxic in a chromosomal-instability, cancer-predisposition syndrome
